ada_sec: Kickoff: I'm collating the PrivEdge isolation checklist for the on-prem hardening window. Focus areas: network policy tightness, KMS handshake observability, RBAC scope reductions, vuln patch canary, and incident escalation hooks. Anything I missed?

tom_infra: Couple of quick notes: make sure the keystore agent can reach OCSP and HSM CA IPs. Last run we left 443 wide which was risky.

rachel_ops: Audit logging requirement: every KMS decrypt must include the caller service-account and pod UID. We had 'unknown' entries from the agent proxy last quarter.

vivek_devsec: For RBAC we'll remove broad clusterrolebindings in the privedge cluster and introduce minimal roles. Example: create a RoleBinding that grants `keystore:decrypt` clusterrole only to `keystore-agent-sa@keystore`.

ada_sec: Good. Please make sure the RoleBinding uses `subject.kind: ServiceAccount` and explicitly references `namespace: keystore`. Avoid referencing Groups.

vivek_devsec: Draft RBAC snippet I will post to the repo:

```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: keystore-decrypt-binding
  namespace: keystore
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: keystore-agent-sa
  namespace: keystore
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: keystore-decrypt
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

tom_infra: Netpol guidance: 1) restrict egress to named IP ranges for HSMs + metrics collector 2) allow only kube-dns svc for DNS 3) deny all other egress by default. We'll publish example YAML: `netpol-privedge-keystore-egress.yaml`.

rachel_ops: For SIEM tagging, add labels `env=privedge` and `component=keystore-agent` to logs. Also, when a decrypt fails log both the error and the `caller_subject` field.

ada_sec: Vulnerability triage: the keystore sidecar upstream glibc fix is available. Plan: build a patched image, run the HSM sim smoke-tests (1000 decrypts), canary to one private pool AZ, measure error rate.

vivek_devsec: Automation: include `tools/canary_kms_test.sh --iterations=1000 --fail-threshold=0.005` in the pipeline. If failures exceed threshold revert.

tom_infra: Important: canary pod must have identical netpol/e2e routing as prod. We had false positives when canary could reach internet but prod couldn't.

rachel_ops: Alerting query to detect KMS regressions: `sum(rate(kms_decrypt_failure_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kms_decrypt_requests_total[5m]))` > 0.005 -> fire P1. Add slack notify `#privedge-sec`.

oncall-bot: privedge-canary job started by tom_infra at 1727003600 status: running.

ada_sec: Runbook decision points: if decrypt error rate >0.5% for >10m -> failover to hosted fallback, flip traffic, and start incident bridge. Also escalate to legal/compliance for any decrypt errors with `principal_type=external`.

vivek_devsec: One more: ensure audit logs include the KMS request ID and HSM return code to correlate. Add `audit.kms.request_id` and `audit.hsm.rc` fields.

tom_infra: I'll upload the netpol and canary manifests to the repo. rachel, can you confirm SIEM index mapping for the new fields?

rachel_ops: Yes, I'll map `audit.kms.request_id` -> `kms.request_id`, `audit.hsm.rc` -> `hsm.return_code`. Retention ask: 90d hot, 2y cold. For auth failures keep 1y hot; I'll file to compliance.

ada_sec: Action items: vivek -> push RBAC PR, tom -> netpol + canary manifests, rachel -> SIEM mapping + runbook edits, I'll coordinate the canary window and incident channel. Sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. :white_check_mark:
